countScope: Completed valid phase rows only, including explicitly labeled historical reference comparisons. Native fine/initialization/recovery checks are counted separately. Invalid coordinate/UI recipes and rejected step attempts are excluded and preserved separately; running phases are not counted in completed totals.

selectedMeasuredFeedback.trajectoryScope: Full traces compared for four force/orientation corners times five noise cohorts. All 350 cases compared using their exact peak-error metrics. Interior full trajectories were not stored.
selectedMeasuredFeedback.controllerInputs: Measured force and magnet position; no programmed surface profile or actual surface acceleration enters the controller.
selectedMeasuredFeedback.qualificationRole: Historical near-contact reference; superseded for the user-confirmed B/S load-cell location.

conditionalLimits: 5–50 N in 5 N steps and 0–90 degrees in 15-degree steps are sampled fixed operating points, with an equilibrium start and this specific smooth 1 mm x 10 mm bump at 100 mm/s.
Four random seeds are actual tested realizations, not a probability bound for arbitrary sensor noise.

The actual B/S two-sensor candidate uses 1.4 kg downstream with exact static gravity tare, calibrated drive and timing, 100 us force/position latency and filter/current response, 10 kHz sampling, 0.02 N force RMS and 1 um S-relative-to-A position RMS.

The original 20 ms gate baseline holds recentering in all saved noisy traces; it demonstrates fast force control and bounded issued normal motion with recentering held. The final 100 ms gate receives its own full qualification.
Mass-model +/-0.2% (2.8 g) passes separate 20 ms-gate corner experiments with exact gravity tare; this does not bound combined calibration errors or gravity-tare errors.
Near-contact studies are historical comparisons and do not qualify the confirmed upstream B/S measurement.
Only measured force/relative position and issued commands enter the force and recentering loops; physical sensor generation and qualification plots can use plant truth.
Unmodeled force-sensor delay, bias, force-constant drift and other coefficient mismatches need separate qualification. One-factor passes do not establish simultaneous worst-case performance.
Numerical passes and spring packaging screens do not establish physical stiffness, cross-axis behavior, thermal capability, fatigue, friction calibration, PWM ripple or sensor performance.
